a.claim: If you change buses then you will normally be charged a new bus fare up to the daily/weekly price cap.

b.claim: You must touch in using the same card on the second bus and the free fare will be applied automatically.

a.claim: These cover the city but exclude sightseeing buses, night buses and the airport - though you can ride the airport bus within the city, say to the zoo.

b.claim: The all-day ticket is a great way to see the city without the expense of the tour buses, as you can get on and off all Lothian buses for the whole day.

a.claim: Travel on the airport tram is free for young people aged 5-26 who have a Young Scot National Entitlement Card issued by Edinburgh Council.

b.claim: Fares and ticketing are integrated with Lothian Buses, with the same fares charged on both systems, except for services to the airport where the tram is more expensive.

a.claim: You can make a change to another bus or a tram free of charge during one hour.

b.claim: Single bus fares paid using Contactless or Oyster cards include a second bus journey within one hour at no extra charge.

a.claim: Food: Food is of great quality everywhere - both fancy sit-down restraunts and lots of sandwiches and hot snacks available everywhere for quite cheap.

b.claim: You can get cheap food in Rome, the problem is that if you don't know the city well or are forced to eat out in the centre, the prices go up.

a.claim: Taxis are comparatively cheap especially at night when there are no traffic jams to be expected.

b.claim: In the daytime, it is not always a good idea to take a taxi, as walking or taking the metro (See: Métro) will be cheaper and, depending on traffic, faster.

a.claim: At these times public transport (and especially the Tube) usually offers the best alternative for speed and reduced hassle.

b.claim: Buses are generally quicker than taking the Tube for short (less than a couple of stops on the Tube) trips, but for longer ones can be much slower especially when traffic is heavy.

a.claim: For sightseeing, buses are a much more pleasant way to travel than the Tube, and cheaper too for a single journey.

b.claim: Buses are generally quicker than taking the Tube for shorter (less than a couple of stops on the Tube) trips, and out of central London you're likely to be closer to a bus stop than a Tube station.

a.claim: Pushing and rushing are seen as extremely rude - there's not much need to run for a Tube train unless it's the very last one of the day!

b.claim: Refrain from walking slowly in tight spaces to avoid annoying any fast walking people that may be trying to pass.

a.claim: Tipping is not generally a thing in Italy, and you should not feel obligated.

b.claim: Waiters have been known to take advantage of patrons by bringing more expensive items than what was ordered or asking for a tip although it's not mandatory and should be included in the price by law.

a.claim: On the other hand, you will probably get the cold shoulder if you stop a random person in the métro, fail to greet them and say "where is place X or street Y".

b.claim: Some of their reputation for brusqueness may stem from the fact that they are constantly surrounded by tourists, who can sometimes themselves seem rude and demanding.

a.claim: St. Peter's in particular is known for rejecting tourists for uncovered knees, shoulders, midriffs, etc.

b.claim: The dress code is strict - no exposed shoulders, no midriffs, no shorts or skirts above the knee.
